metadata.historicalScope: 1666-2026: intellectual antecedents and the principal research programs pursuing general machine intelligence.
metadata.description: A connected research history with dated milestones, documented project durations and explicitly editorial research phases across thirteen strands.
metadata.coverage: Systematic coverage of major research lineages and turning points, not a claim to enumerate every publication, institution or product release.

edgeSemantics.sequence: Editorial reading order within a research strand, not causation, exclusive ancestry or finer ordering among year-dated events.
edgeSemantics.dependency: A concrete continuation, implementation, input or successor relationship described by the linked works.
edgeSemantics.reference: An explicit historical connection, conceptual comparison, synthesis or debate; it need not indicate direct influence.
edgeSemantics.part-of: The source interval groups the target milestone; the connector meets the bar at the milestone date when it lies inside. Membership need not be exclusive and does not imply causation.

intervalSemantics.Research program: A documented project or explicitly bounded development window; read the precision field for approximate boundaries.
intervalSemantics.Research phase: An overlapping editorial synthesis anchored by selected works. Endpoints do not mean a field began or ceased; recent windows stop at the evidence cutoff.

leibniz.title: Leibniz explores combinatorial reasoning
leibniz.define: The 1666 Dissertation on Combinatorial Art explores representing concepts through elements and combinations, within a much earlier intellectual setting than computer science.
leibniz.significance: It belongs to the prehistory of treating reasoning as a manipulable formal process.
leibniz.limitation: This is a conceptual antecedent, not an AGI project or evidence of direct influence on every later computational approach.
leibniz.precision: The marker dates the 1666 dissertation; Leibniz's later projects for a universal language and calculus developed over time.

bayes.title: Bayes and Price publish inverse probability
bayes.define: A posthumous paper studies how observations inform an unknown probability, edited and communicated by Price.
bayes.significance: It is an early foundation for updating beliefs from evidence, later central to probabilistic AI.
bayes.limitation: Modern Bayesian inference incorporates extensive subsequent developments; the original paper is not a modern AI algorithm.
bayes.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

boole.title: Boole algebraizes logic
boole.define: An Investigation of the Laws of Thought develops algebraic treatment of logical relationships.
boole.significance: Formal reasoning becomes amenable to symbolic calculation, providing background for digital logic and automated inference.
boole.limitation: Truth-functional reasoning alone does not supply uncertainty handling, learned knowledge or common sense.
boole.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

frege.title: Frege introduces Begriffsschrift
frege.define: The concept-script develops quantification and function-based logical notation beyond propositional operations.
frege.significance: Relations, objects and quantifiers become explicit ingredients of later knowledge representation and theorem proving.
frege.limitation: Greater expressive power also introduces harder questions of decidability and search; this was a logical system, not a computer program.
frege.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

godel.title: Godel establishes incompleteness
godel.define: The incompleteness results identify limitations of consistent, effectively axiomatized formal systems sufficiently expressive for arithmetic.
godel.significance: General reasoning must distinguish what a particular formal system can establish from what is true or computationally accessible.
godel.limitation: The theorems do not by themselves prove that humans transcend all machines or that AGI is impossible.
godel.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

phase-formal-foundations.title: Formal foundations of machine intelligence
phase-formal-foundations.contributors: Multiple research groups; individual attribution appears in the linked milestones.
phase-formal-foundations.define: Logic, computability, information theory and feedback provide distinct formal tools for thinking about mechanical reasoning and adaptive behavior. Turing connects these developments to an explicit question about machine intelligence.
phase-formal-foundations.significance: The timeline displays the overlapping formation of a problem space, rather than presenting the imitation game without its intellectual background.
phase-formal-foundations.limitation: These works do not constitute one institution or a single agreed theory of intelligence; this interval groups their complementary roles.
phase-formal-foundations.precision: Editorial periodization anchored by the cited milestones. Boundaries identify a reading window, not a field-wide founding or termination date. Year-only boundaries do not claim exact days. The tradition continues beyond this selected phase.
phase-formal-foundations.evidenceType: Editorial synthesis of the linked primary works

church.title: Church formalizes effective computation
church.define: Church uses formal accounts of effective calculability and establishes an unsolvability result for a decision problem of elementary number theory.
church.significance: Together with other equivalent models, this helps define computation precisely and establishes principled limits.
church.limitation: Computational universality does not imply efficient learning, practical solvability or human-level intelligence.
church.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

turing-machine.title: Turing defines universal computation
turing-machine.define: On Computable Numbers models computation with abstract machines, introduces universal-machine reasoning and establishes undecidability results.
turing-machine.significance: A general programmable substrate becomes mathematically describable, separating hardware universality from particular algorithms.
turing-machine.limitation: The paper supplies no general learning mechanism. Universal computation and general intelligence are different claims.
turing-machine.precision: Conventionally dated 1936; publication belongs to the 1936-1937 journal volume.

mcculloch-pitts.title: Formal neurons connect networks and logic
mcculloch-pitts.define: Threshold-like idealized neurons and their connections are used to analyze logical properties of nervous activity.
mcculloch-pitts.significance: This establishes an early connectionist foundation: networks of simple units can implement nontrivial computations.
mcculloch-pitts.limitation: The model is highly abstract and does not include modern gradient training or large-scale empirical learning.
mcculloch-pitts.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

phase-early-neural.title: Early neural computation and learning
phase-early-neural.contributors: Multiple research groups; individual attribution appears in the linked milestones.
phase-early-neural.define: Formal networks, changing connections and trainable classifiers establish several approaches to adaptive computation. The later perceptron debate exposes limitations of particular model classes.
phase-early-neural.significance: Neural learning appears as an extended research tradition with internal alternatives and constraints, not as an invention of the deep-learning era.
phase-early-neural.limitation: A 1969 publication is the selected boundary, not a claim that neural research ended or that its later history followed from one book.
phase-early-neural.precision: Editorial periodization anchored by the cited milestones. Boundaries identify a reading window, not a field-wide founding or termination date. Year-only boundaries do not claim exact days. The tradition continues beyond this selected phase.
phase-early-neural.evidenceType: Editorial synthesis of the linked primary works

ngram-foundation.title: Shannon explores statistical structure in language
ngram-foundation.define: The communication paper uses successive approximations to English to illustrate how conditional structure changes generated sequences.
ngram-foundation.significance: Statistical sequence prediction has a long history before neural language models.
ngram-foundation.limitation: The illustrations concern information and regularities, not a claim that next-token prediction alone proves understanding.
ngram-foundation.precision: Year-level publication or historical milestone; later revisions do not change this marker.

shannon.title: Information theory separates signal and meaning
shannon.define: A Mathematical Theory of Communication formalizes entropy, coding and channel capacity while setting semantic interpretation aside.
shannon.significance: Prediction, compression and information constraints acquire mathematical tools later used throughout machine learning.
shannon.limitation: Predictive efficiency is not automatically semantic understanding; that distinction is built into the original theory's scope.
shannon.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

turing-unorganized.title: Turing investigates unorganized machines
turing-unorganized.define: An unpublished-at-the-time report explores learning machines and networks of simple elements.
turing-unorganized.significance: Neural-style learning is part of the early machine-intelligence agenda before the Dartmouth project.
turing-unorganized.limitation: The report was not publicly published in 1948; its later circulation and publication must be distinguished from composition.
turing-unorganized.precision: 1948 report date; first publication was later, in 1968.

wiener.title: Cybernetics unifies feedback and control
wiener.define: Cybernetics studies communication, feedback and control in animals and machines within a shared mathematical perspective.
wiener.significance: Intelligence can be investigated as a closed loop of action, observation and correction, influencing adaptive and robotic systems.
wiener.limitation: Stable control or adaptive regulation alone does not establish language understanding, abstract reasoning or general competence.
wiener.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

hebb.title: Hebb links learning to changing connections
hebb.define: The Organization of Behavior proposes activity-dependent strengthening and cell assemblies as ingredients of learning and cognition.
hebb.significance: Learning can be understood as changes in a network rather than only the execution of fixed rules.
hebb.limitation: Popular short slogans are later summaries; the book does not give a universal quantitative training algorithm.
hebb.precision: First publication in 1949; the linked publisher record is a later electronic edition.

shannon-chess.title: Chess becomes heuristic search
shannon-chess.define: Programming a Computer for Playing Chess describes evaluation functions and alternative ways to organize game-tree search.
shannon-chess.significance: Search spaces, heuristics and computational budgets become enduring components of intelligent decision systems.
shannon-chess.limitation: A known-rule board game leaves perception, open-world modeling and autonomous goal formation largely outside the task.
shannon-chess.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

turing-test.title: Turing proposes the imitation game
turing-test.define: Computing Machinery and Intelligence reframes machine intelligence through an imitation game and discusses learning, education and child machines.
turing-test.significance: Behavioral evaluation and acquired competence become central alternatives to arguing solely about an undefined act of thinking.
turing-test.limitation: Conversational success is not a complete test of cognition and does not establish consciousness.
turing-test.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

robbins-monro.title: Stochastic approximation enables noisy optimization
robbins-monro.define: Iterative updates estimate a solution when only noisy observations are available.
robbins-monro.significance: Stochastic learning and reinforcement-learning convergence analysis gain a common mathematical foundation.
robbins-monro.limitation: Classical guarantees require conditions on noise, step sizes and functions that practical deep learning need not satisfy.
robbins-monro.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

dartmouth-proposal.title: The Dartmouth AI proposal is submitted
dartmouth-proposal.contributors: John McCarthy; Marvin Minsky; Nathaniel Rochester; Claude Shannon
dartmouth-proposal.define: The proposal names artificial intelligence and sets out language, abstraction, neural networks, computational complexity and self-improvement as research topics.
dartmouth-proposal.significance: A broad machine-intelligence agenda receives a common institutional identity before the following summer's project.
dartmouth-proposal.limitation: A research proposal is not a completed workshop, a working general intelligence or a proof that every proposed goal is achievable.
dartmouth-proposal.precision: Dated publication, public release or event milestone; subsequent revisions and deployments are separate events.

logic-theorist.title: Logic Theorist searches for proofs
logic-theorist.contributors: Allen Newell; Herbert A. Simon; J. Clifford Shaw
logic-theorist.define: The Logic Theory Machine uses symbolic expressions and heuristic search to find proofs in a formal logical domain.
logic-theorist.significance: It demonstrates that computers can manipulate structured symbolic relations, establishing problem solving as an early AI paradigm.
logic-theorist.limitation: Formal proof success depends on a supplied language and problem domain; it does not confer everyday common sense.
logic-theorist.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

phase-early-symbolic.title: Heuristic search and symbolic microworlds
phase-early-symbolic.contributors: Multiple research groups; individual attribution appears in the linked milestones.
phase-early-symbolic.define: Theorem proving, goal-directed search, knowledge representation, language understanding and planning develop through deliberately constrained worlds and explicit representations.
phase-early-symbolic.significance: A sustained attempt to generalize symbolic procedures links early demonstrations to the difficulties of common sense and combinatorial growth.
phase-early-symbolic.limitation: The 1973 boundary marks a historiographical transition associated with evaluation debates; symbolic AI did not stop then.
phase-early-symbolic.precision: Editorial periodization anchored by the cited milestones. Boundaries identify a reading window, not a field-wide founding or termination date. Year-only boundaries do not claim exact days. The tradition continues beyond this selected phase.
phase-early-symbolic.evidenceType: Editorial synthesis of the linked primary works

dartmouth-workshop.title: Dartmouth summer research project
dartmouth-workshop.contributors: John McCarthy; Marvin Minsky; Nathaniel Rochester; Claude Shannon; participating researchers
dartmouth-workshop.define: An extended summer study brings changing groups of researchers together to explore machine intelligence. The 1955 proposal and the 1956 working period are separate historical objects.
dartmouth-workshop.significance: The shared research agenda takes institutional form over weeks of discussion and work, rather than at one instantaneous founding ceremony.
dartmouth-workshop.limitation: Attendance varied, and the participants did not agree on a finished architecture or solve general intelligence.
dartmouth-workshop.precision: Approximate June-August 1956 window, at month precision. Solomonoff's archive contains notes from June through August; these are not exact opening and closing dates or a claim that everyone attended throughout.

bellman.title: Dynamic programming organizes sequential decisions
bellman.define: Dynamic Programming systematizes decomposition of multistage decisions using state descriptions and recursive optimality relations.
bellman.significance: Value functions and optimality recursions become foundations for planning and reinforcement learning.
bellman.limitation: Exact computation requires an adequate model and state representation; large state spaces create severe computational costs.
bellman.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

chomsky.title: Syntactic Structures foregrounds generative structure
chomsky.define: The book develops a formal grammatical approach to language and challenges purely local statistical accounts of syntax.
chomsky.significance: Structured linguistic representation becomes a major counterpart to corpus-based language learning.
chomsky.limitation: A grammatical theory is not a general intelligence system, and later neural evidence must be assessed on its own terms.
chomsky.precision: First publication in 1957; the linked publisher record represents a later edition.

perceptron.title: Rosenblatt develops the perceptron
perceptron.define: The perceptron combines adjustable weights with a learning procedure for pattern discrimination.
perceptron.significance: Connectionist systems move from fixed computational circuits toward decisions learned from examples.
perceptron.limitation: Single-layer representational limitations remain; the 1958 paper is distinct from the 1957 report and subsequent hardware demonstrations.
perceptron.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

advice-taker.title: The Advice Taker proposes common-sense programs
advice-taker.define: Programs with Common Sense describes a program that could accept statements, represent knowledge and reason about actions.
advice-taker.significance: Generality is pursued through extensible knowledge and inference instead of a new hand-coded controller for each task.
advice-taker.limitation: This is an agenda rather than a completed system; common-sense acquisition and resource-bounded inference remain unresolved.

gps.title: General Problem Solver separates goals and operators
gps.contributors: Allen Newell; J. Clifford Shaw; Herbert A. Simon
gps.define: GPS uses means-ends analysis to select operations that reduce differences between a current state and a goal.
gps.significance: The same problem-solving procedure can be reused across formally described tasks.
gps.limitation: Humans still supply representations and operators; procedural generality does not remove combinatorial explosion.
gps.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

samuel.title: Samuel demonstrates learning through checkers
samuel.define: A checkers program improves through experience, evaluation-function adjustment and self-play.
samuel.significance: Search and learning from experience are connected decades before modern deep reinforcement learning.
samuel.limitation: The learning environment has fixed rules and a narrow objective; cross-domain autonomous learning is not demonstrated.
samuel.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

adaline.title: ADALINE learns from numerical error
adaline.define: Adaptive switching circuits use adjustable linear units and error-driven weight updates.
adaline.significance: Learning becomes a repeatable numerical procedure, linking neural methods with adaptive filtering and optimization.
adaline.limitation: Linear units have limited expressive power; nonlinear multilayer learning requires additional mechanisms.
adaline.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

lisp.title: Lisp provides a language for symbolic computation
lisp.define: Recursive Functions of Symbolic Expressions formalizes core Lisp ideas through recursive functions and list-structured expressions.
lisp.significance: Symbolic AI gains a practical medium for interpreters, recursive search and manipulation of program structures.
lisp.limitation: A programming language enables implementations; it is not itself a theory or realization of intelligence.
lisp.precision: The paper appeared in April 1960; language development began earlier, around 1958.

phase-universal-agents.title: Universal induction and ideal general agents
phase-universal-agents.contributors: Multiple research groups; individual attribution appears in the linked milestones.
phase-universal-agents.define: Algorithmic probability and description complexity inform formal models of general prediction, sequential decision-making, self-rewriting and intelligence measurement.
phase-universal-agents.significance: A long-running mathematical program supplies reference ideals against which computability and resource constraints can be made explicit.
phase-universal-agents.limitation: Formal optimality under assumptions is not a practical implementation or experimental demonstration of human-level generality.
phase-universal-agents.precision: Editorial periodization anchored by the cited milestones. Boundaries identify a reading window, not a field-wide founding or termination date. Year-only boundaries do not claim exact days. The tradition continues beyond this selected phase.
phase-universal-agents.evidenceType: Editorial synthesis of the linked primary works

solomonoff.title: Algorithmic probability formalizes induction
solomonoff.define: A formal theory of inductive inference weights candidate explanations using program descriptions and their lengths.
solomonoff.significance: Induction, prediction, compression and universal computation become connected in a mathematical framework.
solomonoff.limitation: The ideal universal distribution is not computable in general and depends on a description framework; it is not an executable AGI.
solomonoff.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

dendral.title: DENDRAL begins knowledge-intensive scientific inference
dendral.contributors: Edward Feigenbaum; Joshua Lederberg; Bruce Buchanan and collaborators
dendral.define: The project combines chemical constraints and search to infer molecular structures.
dendral.significance: Domain knowledge becomes a way to control search and achieve useful expert performance, helping establish knowledge engineering.
dendral.limitation: The project develops over years; a strong chemistry system does not establish general intelligence.
dendral.precision: 1965 marks the project's beginning, not completion of every later DENDRAL result.

good.title: Good considers an intelligence explosion
good.define: Good discusses a conditional scenario in which a sufficiently capable machine improves machine design, potentially enabling further improvement.
good.significance: Recursive improvement and the control of advanced machines enter the research discussion early.
good.limitation: This is a conditional argument, not an observed runaway process or a dated prediction of when it must occur.
good.precision: The reproduced original carries a 1965 copyright, retained as this marker; the current publisher and DOI record instead date the chapter to 1966. The text also notes an April 1963 first draft.

kolmogorov.title: Kolmogorov defines description-based complexity
kolmogorov.define: Information content is related to the length of an effective description rather than only a probability distribution.
kolmogorov.significance: Algorithmic information becomes a shared language for compression, induction and theoretical intelligence.
kolmogorov.limitation: Exact Kolmogorov complexity is not computable; practical compression is an approximation, not the ideal quantity.
kolmogorov.precision: The marker dates the original 1965 Russian paper; its English translation appeared in 1968.

phase-knowledge-engineering.title: Knowledge engineering and expert systems
phase-knowledge-engineering.contributors: Multiple research groups; individual attribution appears in the linked milestones.
phase-knowledge-engineering.define: Knowledge-intensive scientific inference develops into rule-based consultation and configuration. Common-sense projects expand the intended scope while operational experience reveals acquisition and maintenance costs.
phase-knowledge-engineering.significance: The phase connects useful specialist performance, labor-intensive knowledge construction and the limits of transferring expertise across domains.
phase-knowledge-engineering.limitation: The window includes uneven adoption and commercial contraction; it does not imply that every expert system failed or disappeared in 1993.
phase-knowledge-engineering.precision: Editorial periodization anchored by the cited milestones. Boundaries identify a reading window, not a field-wide founding or termination date. Year-only boundaries do not claim exact days. The tradition continues beyond this selected phase.
phase-knowledge-engineering.evidenceType: Editorial synthesis of the linked primary works

robinson.title: Resolution makes theorem proving systematic
robinson.define: Resolution and unification organize first-order logical inference into mechanically executable proof search.
robinson.significance: They become central components of automated reasoning, logic programming and later learning-guided provers.
robinson.limitation: Sound inference rules do not guarantee finding a proof within available resources; first-order reasoning has fundamental decision limits.
robinson.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

alpac.title: ALPAC evaluates machine translation progress
alpac.define: Language and Machines assesses translation quality, cost and research progress, favoring further basic work and supporting tools.
alpac.significance: Funding and evaluation become visible forces shaping the direction of language research.
alpac.limitation: The report concerns a particular policy and research context; it is not evidence that all AI research stopped worldwide.
alpac.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

eliza.title: ELIZA exposes the appearance of understanding
eliza.define: ELIZA generates responses through pattern matching and transformation rules; the DOCTOR script supports a therapy-like dialogue.
eliza.significance: Users' interpretations reveal how readily conversational form can suggest understanding.
eliza.limitation: Scripted responsiveness does not supply open-world knowledge or general reasoning, and perceived understanding is not an adequate capability measure.
eliza.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

phase-early-critique.title: Translation and generality claims face sustained scrutiny
phase-early-critique.contributors: Multiple research groups; individual attribution appears in the linked milestones.
phase-early-critique.define: Reports and critiques question translation progress, model limitations, formal accounts of expertise and generalization beyond restricted tasks.
phase-early-critique.significance: The interval shows how several distinct lines of criticism accumulate before later narratives group funding contractions into an AI winter.
phase-early-critique.limitation: This is an editorial scrutiny window, not a worldwide funding interval. Countries, funders and technical communities followed different trajectories.
phase-early-critique.precision: Editorial periodization anchored by the cited milestones. Boundaries identify a reading window, not a field-wide founding or termination date. Year-only boundaries do not claim exact days. The tradition continues beyond this selected phase.
phase-early-critique.evidenceType: Editorial synthesis of the linked primary works

shakey.title: Shakey research and development
shakey.contributors: Charles Rosen; Nils Nilsson; Peter Hart; the SRI team
shakey.define: The SRI project integrates visual perception, world representation, planning and mobile action through repeated engineering and experiments. Search and planning methods develop within this sustained effort.
shakey.significance: Embodied intelligence becomes an integration problem involving several interacting components, with identifiable technical results produced during the project.
shakey.limitation: The controlled rooms and tasks differ substantially from open-world robotics; the project did not establish unrestricted general intelligence.
shakey.precision: SRI dates Shakey development to 1966-1972. Both boundaries retain year precision; they are project dates, not the lifetime of the underlying research ideas.

astar.title: A-star formalizes heuristic path search
astar.contributors: Peter Hart; Nils Nilsson; Bertram Raphael
astar.define: Heuristic estimates guide graph search while supporting optimality under stated conditions.
astar.significance: Problem-solving search gains reusable principles for navigation, planning and later learned heuristics.
astar.limitation: Optimality conditions and heuristic quality matter; worst-case search remains costly.
astar.precision: Year-level publication or historical milestone; later revisions do not change this marker.

frame-problem.title: The frame problem challenges action representation
frame-problem.define: The work examines how a reasoning system can represent what changes and what persists when an action occurs.
frame-problem.significance: It reveals that possessing a logical language does not make common-sense dynamics easy to represent or compute.
frame-problem.limitation: Formal, computational and philosophical versions differ; no single simple rule resolves all of them.
frame-problem.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

perceptrons.title: Perceptron limitations become a major debate
perceptrons.define: Perceptrons analyzes mathematical limits of particular classes of neural classifiers.
perceptrons.significance: Representation, learnability and practical training must be distinguished rather than treated as interchangeable.
perceptrons.limitation: The book does not prove that all neural networks are useless; later funding changes cannot be assigned to this book alone.
perceptrons.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

backprop-linnainmaa.title: Reverse-mode differentiation is systematized
backprop-linnainmaa.define: Work on differentiating computational procedures develops a general reverse accumulation method.
backprop-linnainmaa.significance: A numerical foundation later used for neural backpropagation is established independently of its eventual popularization.
backprop-linnainmaa.limitation: The history of automatic differentiation and its adoption for neural learning should not be collapsed into one invention.
backprop-linnainmaa.precision: The marker is the 1970 thesis; the linked journal treatment appeared in 1976.

cook.title: Complexity theory explains difficult search
cook.define: The complexity of theorem-proving procedures establishes a foundational completeness result for satisfiability.
cook.significance: Formalizing a problem does not eliminate its worst-case computational difficulty, motivating heuristics and approximation.
cook.limitation: Worst-case hardness does not make every instance hard and does not imply that intelligence is impossible.
cook.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

shrdlu.title: SHRDLU understands a blocks microworld
shrdlu.define: SHRDLU combines language analysis, world knowledge, inference and action planning in a controlled blocks environment.
shrdlu.significance: It demonstrates how language can connect to state and action while exposing the importance of environmental assumptions.
shrdlu.limitation: Rich behavior inside a microworld does not directly scale to unrestricted everyday understanding.
shrdlu.precision: The marker is the 1971 MIT report; the 1972 publication is a later presentation of the work.

strips.title: STRIPS formalizes action planning
strips.define: Actions are described with preconditions and changes to a symbolic state, allowing search for goal-achieving sequences.
strips.significance: A lasting representation for classical planning emerges from robotics research.
strips.limitation: Deterministic, well-specified states simplify the task; real execution requires perception, monitoring and recovery.
strips.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

dreyfus.title: Dreyfus criticizes formalized accounts of expertise
dreyfus.define: What Computers Can't Do challenges assumptions that everyday skilled behavior can be captured through explicit formal rules alone.
dreyfus.significance: Situated knowledge, embodiment and background understanding become enduring objections to narrow symbolic accounts.
dreyfus.limitation: Philosophical critique does not establish an impossibility theorem for every future computational architecture.
dreyfus.precision: The marker dates the 1972 original; the linked expanded retrospective edition appeared in 1992.

prolog.title: Prolog makes logic executable
prolog.contributors: Alain Colmerauer; Philippe Roussel and collaborators
prolog.define: Prolog develops from work on language processing and automated deduction, expressing programs through relations and queries.
prolog.significance: Knowledge descriptions and proof search become closely connected in a programming interface.
prolog.limitation: Declarative meaning and operational search order differ; a logical program still requires control and resource choices.
prolog.precision: 1972 marks early development; the linked 1993 account is a retrospective by its creators.

lighthill.title: The Lighthill report criticizes AI generalization
lighthill.define: The report challenges broad AI promises and emphasizes combinatorial explosion in the context of British research policy.
lighthill.significance: Small demonstrations versus scalable capability becomes a consequential funding and methodological dispute.
lighthill.limitation: AI winters are retrospective, uneven periods across countries and fields, not a single worldwide shutdown.
lighthill.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

pomdp.title: Partially observable decisions use belief states
pomdp.define: The work studies optimal control when the underlying state is only indirectly observed.
pomdp.significance: Decision making can explicitly represent uncertainty about the world, connecting probability with sequential action.
pomdp.limitation: Belief-state planning becomes expensive in large spaces; an exact formulation does not ensure practical tractability.
pomdp.precision: Year-level publication or historical milestone; later revisions do not change this marker.

frames.title: Frames organize structured background knowledge
frames.define: Frames represent situations through structured slots and default information, addressing what ordinary understanding leaves unstated.
frames.significance: Knowledge representation expands beyond isolated rules toward reusable situational structures.
frames.limitation: Defaults can conflict, and automatic acquisition and composition of frames remain difficult.
frames.precision: The 1974 MIT memo precedes a 1975 book-chapter version.

werbos.title: Werbos studies gradient learning in multilayer systems
werbos.define: The doctoral work explores backward differentiation for nonlinear modeling and learning.
werbos.significance: Numerical differentiation becomes connected to the problem of training internal representations.
werbos.limitation: Earlier differentiation work and later independent neural applications remain part of the history; no single date captures the entire development.
werbos.precision: 1974 doctoral thesis; later publications and popularization are separate stages.

holland.title: Genetic adaptation becomes a computational framework
holland.define: Adaptation in Natural and Artificial Systems develops population-based search through selection and inherited variation.
holland.significance: Evolution supplies a distinct optimization route later applied to networks, representations and environments.
holland.limitation: An evolutionary metaphor does not ensure efficient discovery; encoding and fitness design constrain what can emerge.
holland.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

phase-open-ended.title: Evolutionary search and learning to learn
phase-open-ended.contributors: Multiple research groups; individual attribution appears in the linked milestones.
phase-open-ended.define: Evolutionary adaptation, changing network structure, meta-learning and novelty-driven exploration develop alternatives to learning a single fixed task under a fixed objective.
phase-open-ended.significance: The interval connects a long-standing search for adaptation mechanisms with later work on generated curricula and open-ended environments.
phase-open-ended.limitation: The grouping is conceptual and overlapping, not evidence that every later method directly descends from each earlier one.
phase-open-ended.precision: Editorial periodization anchored by the cited milestones. Boundaries identify a reading window, not a field-wide founding or termination date. Year-only boundaries do not claim exact days. The tradition continues beyond this selected phase.
phase-open-ended.evidenceType: Editorial synthesis of the linked primary works

mycin.title: MYCIN demonstrates rule-based expert consultation
mycin.contributors: Edward Shortliffe; Bruce Buchanan and collaborators
mycin.define: MYCIN investigates medical consultation through production rules, certainty factors and explanatory reasoning.
mycin.significance: Knowledge engineering and uncertainty handling support useful specialist performance.
mycin.limitation: A research system is distinct from routine clinical deployment; knowledge acquisition and maintenance limit extension.
mycin.precision: The 1976 monograph marks a mature account of a project begun earlier.

physical-symbol.title: The physical symbol system hypothesis is stated
physical-symbol.define: Their Turing Award lecture argues for a relationship between physical symbol systems and general intelligent action, alongside heuristic search.
physical-symbol.significance: Symbolic AI receives an explicit general-intelligence hypothesis linking computer programs and cognition.
physical-symbol.limitation: The authors present an empirical hypothesis, not a proved necessary-and-sufficient theorem about all possible intelligence.
physical-symbol.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

em.title: Expectation-maximization learns with latent variables
em.contributors: Arthur Dempster; Nan Laird; Donald Rubin
em.define: EM alternates inference about missing or latent quantities with parameter updates.
em.significance: Probabilistic models gain a reusable training procedure, influencing speech, mixtures and representation learning.
em.limitation: Local optima, identifiability and modeling assumptions remain constraints.
em.precision: Year-level publication or historical milestone; later revisions do not change this marker.

mdl.title: Minimum description length links modeling and compression
mdl.define: Modeling is framed as balancing the description length of a model and its encoded data.
mdl.significance: Compression becomes a practical principle for selecting explanations and controlling complexity.
mdl.limitation: The coding scheme and model class matter; compactness alone does not establish causal truth.
mdl.precision: Year-level publication or historical milestone; later revisions do not change this marker.

chinese-room.title: The Chinese Room challenges computational understanding
chinese-room.define: The thought experiment questions whether following formal symbol rules is sufficient for understanding.
chinese-room.significance: Behavior, semantics, consciousness and functional competence become explicitly separable issues in AI debate.
chinese-room.limitation: This is a philosophical argument rather than a performance experiment or a direct engineering impossibility theorem.
chinese-room.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

neocognitron.title: The Neocognitron learns hierarchical visual patterns
neocognitron.define: A layered network uses local receptive fields and alternating processing stages to recognize patterns despite positional variation.
neocognitron.significance: It is an important predecessor of later convolutional visual architectures.
neocognitron.limitation: Its learning mechanisms differ from modern end-to-end backpropagation; architectural ancestry does not mean algorithmic identity.
neocognitron.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

nonmonotonic.title: Nonmonotonic logic models revisable conclusions
nonmonotonic.contributors: Raymond Reiter; John McCarthy and other researchers
nonmonotonic.define: Default logic and circumscription formalize reasoning in which new evidence can withdraw earlier conclusions.
nonmonotonic.significance: Common-sense exceptions can be expressed beyond classical monotonic deduction.
nonmonotonic.limitation: Different formalisms have different semantics and computational costs; common sense is not solved by adding defaults alone.
nonmonotonic.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

r1.title: R1 configures computer systems with expert rules
r1.define: R1 applies production-system knowledge to configuring computer orders.
r1.significance: Expert systems move from laboratory demonstrations into economically useful organizational work.
r1.limitation: Knowledge acquisition, maintenance and changing product constraints limit how broadly the approach transfers.
r1.precision: Year-level publication or historical milestone; later revisions do not change this marker.

fifth-generation.title: Japan launches the Fifth Generation project
fifth-generation.define: The program invests in knowledge processing, logic programming and parallel inference machines.
fifth-generation.significance: General-intelligence ambitions become tied to national research policy and proposed hardware architectures.
fifth-generation.limitation: Program initiation is not goal attainment; scientific results and later commercial impact require separate assessment.
fifth-generation.precision: The principal program began in 1982 and ran through 1992.

hopfield.title: Hopfield networks model associative memory
hopfield.define: Recurrent networks with an energy-based description retrieve patterns through dynamical convergence.
hopfield.significance: Neural computation connects to statistical physics, optimization and attractor dynamics.
hopfield.limitation: Storage capacity, spurious attractors and convergence conditions limit the model's role as a general memory system.
hopfield.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

phase-connectionism.title: Connectionist revival and trainable representations
phase-connectionism.contributors: Multiple research groups; individual attribution appears in the linked milestones.
phase-connectionism.define: Associative and probabilistic networks, gradient-trained internal representations, recurrence and convolution develop in parallel, producing increasingly practical learning systems.
phase-connectionism.significance: The interval shows repeated work on optimization, memory and inductive structure behind later large-scale learning.
phase-connectionism.limitation: The chosen milestones do not establish a single invention date for backpropagation or a period when other research traditions disappeared.
phase-connectionism.precision: Editorial periodization anchored by the cited milestones. Boundaries identify a reading window, not a field-wide founding or termination date. Year-only boundaries do not claim exact days. The tradition continues beyond this selected phase.
phase-connectionism.evidenceType: Editorial synthesis of the linked primary works

program-fgcs.title: Fifth Generation Computer Systems project
program-fgcs.contributors: ICOT and participating Japanese and international researchers
program-fgcs.define: A decade-long national research program develops logic-programming-based parallel inference systems, associated architectures and software. Its 1982 launch remains a separate point event.
program-fgcs.significance: Symbolic inference is pursued through a coordinated combination of hardware, programming language and application research.
program-fgcs.limitation: Project completion does not establish general intelligence. The main project must be distinguished from the subsequent software-portability and dissemination work.
program-fgcs.precision: ICOT states that the main FGCS project ran from 1982 to its conclusion in 1992. The later follow-on effort and March 1995 closure are not folded into this bar.

act.title: ACT systematizes a cognitive architecture
act.define: The Architecture of Cognition develops an account of knowledge, production rules and learning mechanisms.
act.significance: A shared architecture aims to explain performance across tasks, including human errors and timing.
act.limitation: Explaining human cognition is not identical to maximizing benchmark accuracy; this version predates later ACT-R systems.
act.precision: The 1983 first edition is the milestone; later electronic editions have different publication dates.

phase-cognitive-integration.title: Cognitive architectures and explicit AGI integration
phase-cognitive-integration.contributors: Multiple research groups; individual attribution appears in the linked milestones.
phase-cognitive-integration.define: Integrated architectures pursue memory, reasoning, learning and action as interacting functions. Resource-bounded reasoning and the explicit AGI community add alternative formulations of generality.
phase-cognitive-integration.significance: The interval preserves a continuous integrative agenda that would be obscured by a history organized only around benchmark-winning predictors.
phase-cognitive-integration.limitation: The first AGI conference marks a community milestone, not the end of cognitive architecture work or agreement on one implementation.
phase-cognitive-integration.precision: Editorial periodization anchored by the cited milestones. Boundaries identify a reading window, not a field-wide founding or termination date. Year-only boundaries do not claim exact days. The tradition continues beyond this selected phase.
phase-cognitive-integration.evidenceType: Editorial synthesis of the linked primary works

cyc.title: Cyc begins large-scale common-sense knowledge engineering
cyc.define: Cyc attempts to encode concepts, facts and inference rules underlying everyday reasoning.
cyc.significance: It directly addresses the missing background knowledge that limits narrow expert systems.
cyc.limitation: Manual acquisition, ambiguity, maintenance and grounding remain difficult at scale.
cyc.precision: 1984 marks project initiation; the linked article is Lenat's 1995 account.

expert-maintenance.title: R1's maintainers report the cost of sustained expertise
expert-maintenance.define: R1 Revisited examines several years of developing and maintaining a deployed expert system.
expert-maintenance.significance: Operational experience reveals why a demonstration is different from a durable knowledge service.
expert-maintenance.limitation: This is a specific maintenance history, not a single cause or start date for a global AI winter.
expert-maintenance.precision: Year-level publication or historical milestone; later revisions do not change this marker.

pac.title: PAC learning formalizes learnability
pac.define: A Theory of the Learnable frames learning in terms of accuracy, probability, sample requirements and computation.
pac.significance: Claims about learning can be related to explicit assumptions and resource bounds.
pac.limitation: The assumed distribution and hypothesis class do not automatically cover open-ended real-world adaptation.
pac.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

phase-commercial-reassessment.title: Expert-system maintenance and commercial reassessment
phase-commercial-reassessment.contributors: Multiple research groups; individual attribution appears in the linked milestones.
phase-commercial-reassessment.define: Practical knowledge-maintenance experience and changing computing markets expose limits of scaling specialized AI businesses. Some large research programs continue while parts of the commercial ecosystem contract.
phase-commercial-reassessment.significance: The interval places the second AI-winter narrative within a mixed technical and institutional history instead of depicting a universal research shutdown.
phase-commercial-reassessment.limitation: The selected 1984-1993 evidence window is not a claim that every AI firm or research budget contracted for exactly these years.
phase-commercial-reassessment.precision: Editorial periodization anchored by the cited milestones. Boundaries identify a reading window, not a field-wide founding or termination date. Year-only boundaries do not claim exact days. The tradition continues beyond this selected phase.
phase-commercial-reassessment.evidenceType: Editorial synthesis of the linked primary works

phase-statistical-learning.title: Statistical learning and probabilistic inference mature
phase-statistical-learning.contributors: Multiple research groups; individual attribution appears in the linked milestones.
phase-statistical-learning.define: Formal learning guarantees, graphical models, latent-state inference, margin methods and learned language representations strengthen data-based approaches. Causal models distinguish intervention from prediction.
phase-statistical-learning.significance: The duration makes visible the methodological groundwork that develops alongside cognitive architectures and neural research.
phase-statistical-learning.limitation: This grouping brings together distinct theoretical commitments; probabilistic inference, causal reasoning and predictive learning are not interchangeable.
phase-statistical-learning.precision: Editorial periodization anchored by the cited milestones. Boundaries identify a reading window, not a field-wide founding or termination date. Year-only boundaries do not claim exact days. The tradition continues beyond this selected phase.
phase-statistical-learning.evidenceType: Editorial synthesis of the linked primary works

boltzmann.title: Boltzmann machines learn probabilistic representations
boltzmann.contributors: David Ackley; Geoffrey Hinton; Terrence Sejnowski
boltzmann.define: Stochastic energy-based networks learn structure involving visible and hidden variables.
boltzmann.significance: Unsupervised representation learning connects neural networks with statistical mechanics and probabilistic modeling.
boltzmann.limitation: Sampling and optimization can be costly; expressive models are not necessarily easy to train.
boltzmann.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

backprop.title: Backpropagation popularizes learned internal representations
backprop.contributors: David Rumelhart; Geoffrey Hinton; Ronald Williams
backprop.define: The 1986 paper demonstrates training multilayer networks by propagating derivatives backward.
backprop.significance: Hidden features become learned rather than entirely specified, contributing to the connectionist revival.
backprop.limitation: This is a major dissemination and demonstration milestone, not the first discovery of reverse differentiation.
backprop.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

brooks.title: Subsumption organizes embodied behavior
brooks.define: Layered behavior-based robot control reduces reliance on a single complete central world model.
brooks.significance: It challenges a rigid perceive-model-plan-act pipeline and advances situated robotics.
brooks.limitation: Reactive competence alone does not provide abstract planning or broad transfer; hybrid approaches remain possible.
brooks.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

society-mind.title: The Society of Mind proposes cooperating mechanisms
society-mind.define: The book explains complex cognition through interactions among many comparatively simple processes.
society-mind.significance: It provides a conceptual alternative to searching for one homogeneous mechanism of intelligence.
society-mind.limitation: It is not a uniformly evaluated executable AGI; comparisons with modern agent teams are thematic rather than direct equivalence.
society-mind.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

schmidhuber-meta.title: Early work studies learning to learn
schmidhuber-meta.define: The diploma thesis investigates systems that can reflect on and modify aspects of their learning processes.
schmidhuber-meta.significance: Learning mechanisms themselves become possible objects of optimization.
schmidhuber-meta.limitation: Theoretical proposals and small experiments are not evidence of unrestricted recursive self-improvement.
schmidhuber-meta.precision: 1987 diploma thesis; later terminology should not inflate the original demonstrations.

soar.title: Soar presents an architecture for general intelligence
soar.contributors: John Laird; Allen Newell; Paul Rosenbloom
soar.define: Soar integrates problem spaces, production rules and chunking within a general cognitive architecture.
soar.significance: Reasoning, action selection and experience-based learning are developed as parts of a lasting integrated system.
soar.limitation: Architectural breadth does not itself demonstrate open-world human-level performance.
soar.precision: The representative paper dates to 1987; the project began around 1983.

fodor-pylyshyn.title: Systematicity challenges connectionist cognition
fodor-pylyshyn.define: The critique asks whether connectionist models can explain the compositional and systematic character of thought.
fodor-pylyshyn.significance: Relations among symbols, distributed representations and compositional generalization become a persistent research dispute.
fodor-pylyshyn.limitation: The argument concerns explanatory adequacy; it does not settle the capabilities of every later neural architecture.
fodor-pylyshyn.precision: Year-level publication or historical milestone; later revisions do not change this marker.

pearl.title: Bayesian networks organize uncertain reasoning
pearl.define: Probabilistic Reasoning in Intelligent Systems develops graphical representations of conditional dependence and inference.
pearl.significance: Uncertain knowledge can be composed and updated systematically rather than handled only through ad hoc rules.
pearl.limitation: Statistical dependence is not automatically causation; network structure and probabilities must still be obtained.
pearl.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

phase-rl-foundations.title: Reinforcement learning and temporal abstraction
phase-rl-foundations.contributors: Multiple research groups; individual attribution appears in the linked milestones.
phase-rl-foundations.define: Prediction errors, action values, learned models, policy gradients and temporally extended skills become a connected toolkit for learning through interaction.
phase-rl-foundations.significance: The period links foundational updates to planning, self-play and hierarchical action over more than a decade of development.
phase-rl-foundations.limitation: Convergence guarantees and demonstrations retain their own assumptions; this is not one universal solution to exploration or long-horizon credit assignment.
phase-rl-foundations.precision: Editorial periodization anchored by the cited milestones. Boundaries identify a reading window, not a field-wide founding or termination date. Year-only boundaries do not claim exact days. The tradition continues beyond this selected phase.
phase-rl-foundations.evidenceType: Editorial synthesis of the linked primary works

td.title: Temporal-difference learning updates predictions
td.define: Learning uses differences between successive predictions instead of waiting exclusively for a final observed outcome.
td.significance: Bootstrapped value learning becomes a central mechanism for decisions with delayed rewards.
td.limitation: Function approximation, off-policy learning and bootstrapping can interact unstably; simple settings do not guarantee general convergence.
td.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

hmm-speech.title: Hidden Markov models systematize speech recognition
hmm-speech.define: A tutorial consolidates probabilistic sequence modeling with hidden states, inference and parameter estimation for speech.
hmm-speech.significance: Uncertainty and temporal structure become a practical industrial learning paradigm before deep sequence models.
hmm-speech.limitation: Conditional independence and state assumptions simplify speech; they do not model all language or cognition.
hmm-speech.precision: This is a consolidation milestone, not the invention date of hidden Markov models.

lenet-early.title: Convolution and gradients recognize handwritten codes
lenet-early.define: Local connections, shared weights and backpropagation are combined for handwritten zip-code recognition.
lenet-early.significance: Useful visual inductive structure is joined with learned representations.
lenet-early.limitation: Success on a bounded recognition task does not imply general language, reasoning or action abilities.
lenet-early.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

program-deep-blue.title: IBM chess research through the Deep Blue victory
program-deep-blue.contributors: Feng-hsiung Hsu; Murray Campbell; Joe Hoane; the IBM team
program-deep-blue.define: After researchers join IBM in 1989, chess-specific search, evaluation and specialized computing develop through successive systems and matches, culminating in the May 1997 Kasparov rematch.
program-deep-blue.significance: The victory becomes the endpoint of a sustained engineering program rather than an isolated event, clarifying the role of search, domain knowledge and computing resources.
program-deep-blue.limitation: This is the IBM development-to-victory window. Earlier ChipTest and Deep Thought work predates it; chess strength alone does not establish general intelligence.
program-deep-blue.precision: The start is the 1989 move to IBM described in its institutional history. The end is the final match day, not an asserted exact project shutdown date.

q-learning.title: Q-learning estimates action values
q-learning.define: The doctoral work develops learning of action values without requiring an explicit transition model.
q-learning.significance: Trial-and-error experience can support long-term decision making, later supplying the algorithmic foundation for DQN.
q-learning.limitation: Theoretical guarantees need assumptions; replacing tables with arbitrary neural networks changes the problem.
q-learning.precision: The thesis dates to 1989; the linked convergence paper appeared in 1992.

brown-smt.title: Statistical machine translation learns from corpora
brown-smt.define: Translation is framed through probabilistic correspondences estimated from bilingual data.
brown-smt.significance: Language engineering moves toward corpus-based estimation before the neural language-model era.
brown-smt.limitation: Statistical association alone struggles with structure and domain shift; training data strongly shape performance.
brown-smt.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

dyna.title: Dyna combines acting learning and planning
dyna.define: An agent learns from actual experience and also uses a learned model to generate updates from simulated experience.
dyna.significance: Direct reinforcement learning and model-based planning become parts of one architecture.
dyna.limitation: Model errors can distort imagined experience; success in simulation needs validation against the actual environment.
dyna.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

elman.title: Recurrent networks learn temporal structure
elman.define: A simple recurrent network carries context between steps while learning sequential regularities.
elman.significance: Learned state becomes a mechanism for representing history in language and other sequences.
elman.limitation: Long-range credit assignment remains difficult, and a recurrent state does not guarantee systematic conceptual composition.
elman.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

grounding.title: The symbol grounding problem is formulated
grounding.define: The paper asks how symbols acquire meaning without relying indefinitely on other uninterpreted symbols.
grounding.significance: Perception, categorization and interaction become central to debates about semantic understanding.
grounding.limitation: The necessary conditions for grounding remain disputed, and sensor access alone is not a sufficient explanation.
grounding.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

brooks-no-representation.title: Intelligence without representation challenges central models
brooks-no-representation.define: The paper argues for situated, embodied systems built through interaction and layered behavior.
brooks-no-representation.significance: Embodiment becomes an explicit challenge to treating intelligence as detached symbol processing.
brooks-no-representation.limitation: The argument does not show that internal models or abstraction are never useful; later systems often combine both approaches.
brooks-no-representation.precision: Year-level publication or historical milestone; later revisions do not change this marker.

reinforce.title: REINFORCE estimates policy gradients
reinforce.define: Stochastic decision networks can be updated using reward-weighted gradient estimators.
reinforce.significance: Direct policy optimization gains a foundation later combined with neural networks and variance-reduction methods.
reinforce.limitation: High variance, sparse rewards and long-horizon credit assignment remain major obstacles.
reinforce.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

td-gammon.title: TD-Gammon learns evaluation through self-play
td-gammon.define: A neural value function improves at backgammon through temporal-difference learning and self-play.
td-gammon.significance: Function approximation and reinforcement learning achieve strong game performance well before deep RL.
td-gammon.limitation: Backgammon's stochastic structure matters; the result does not establish equal effectiveness in every decision problem.
td-gammon.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

act-r.title: ACT-R combines symbolic and subsymbolic cognition
act-r.define: Rules of the Mind develops a cognitive account combining productions with quantitative activation and learning mechanisms.
act-r.significance: Structured knowledge and statistical effects on its use become parts of a hybrid architecture.
act-r.limitation: Human cognitive explanation and engineering task performance remain related but distinct evaluation goals.
act-r.precision: The marker dates the 1993 first edition of Rules of the Mind, not its later electronic reissue.

symbolics-chapter11.title: Symbolics enters Chapter 11
symbolics-chapter11.define: The specialized Lisp-machine company enters bankruptcy protection amid a changing computing market.
symbolics-chapter11.significance: The event anchors one commercial aspect of the uneven contraction often called the second AI winter.
symbolics-chapter11.limitation: It is not the beginning or end of all AI research; statistical learning and other fields continue to grow.
symbolics-chapter11.precision: The Chapter 11 petition was filed on January 27, 1993; the source reproduces a later court motion describing that filing.

bdi.title: BDI agents organize beliefs desires and intentions
bdi.define: The work connects practical agent architectures with explicit representations of beliefs, objectives and commitments.
bdi.significance: Persistent intentions and action organization offer another route to integrated intelligent behavior.
bdi.limitation: The architecture relies on supplied knowledge and plans; it does not automatically learn every component.
bdi.precision: Year-level publication or historical milestone; later revisions do not change this marker.

nars.title: NARS starts from insufficient knowledge and resources
nars.define: The dissertation develops a non-axiomatic reasoning approach centered on adaptation under limited knowledge and computational resources.
nars.significance: It supplies a general-intelligence route contrasting with ideal agents defined by unlimited computation.
nars.limitation: A theory of adaptation and its prototypes do not establish complete human-level capability.
nars.precision: 1995 dissertation milestone; later NAL and OpenNARS versions continue the research.

svm.title: Support-vector machines link margins and generalization
svm.define: Maximum-margin classification and kernel methods support learning in rich feature spaces.
svm.significance: Statistical machine learning becomes a powerful alternative to constructing complete reasoning systems.
svm.limitation: Features, kernels and problem definitions remain consequential; a classifier is not a complete cognitive architecture.
svm.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

robbins-proof.title: EQP proves the Robbins conjecture
robbins-proof.define: Automated equational reasoning produces a proof resolving the Robbins conjecture.
robbins-proof.significance: Search-based symbolic systems contribute a new mathematical result, predating modern language-model mathematics.
robbins-proof.limitation: A landmark in a formal domain does not establish unrestricted mathematical creativity or understanding.
robbins-proof.precision: 1996 proof discovery; the journal account appeared in 1997.

lstm.title: LSTM improves long-range sequence learning
lstm.define: Gates and memory cells help recurrent networks retain and learn information across longer temporal dependencies.
lstm.significance: The architecture becomes important in speech, translation and sequence modeling.
lstm.limitation: Memory is neither unlimited nor automatically reliable; training, capacity and task distribution still matter.
lstm.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

deep-blue.title: Deep Blue wins the Kasparov rematch
deep-blue.define: The specialized chess system wins the six-game rematch by combining large-scale search, chess knowledge and engineering.
deep-blue.significance: A prominent intellectual task reaches superhuman competitive performance, changing public expectations.
deep-blue.limitation: Chess strength does not establish broad intelligence, and the event date differs from later technical publications.
deep-blue.precision: Dated publication, public release or event milestone; subsequent revisions and deployments are separate events.

lenet5.title: LeNet-5 demonstrates practical gradient-based recognition
lenet5.contributors: Yann LeCun; Leon Bottou; Yoshua Bengio; Patrick Haffner
lenet5.define: Gradient-Based Learning Applied to Document Recognition describes convolutional networks and trainable systems for document tasks.
lenet5.significance: It shows that practical neural deployment predates the 2012 deep-learning breakthrough.
lenet5.limitation: A mature application system still differs from broad cognitive or autonomous capability.
lenet5.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

options.title: Options formalize temporal abstraction
options.contributors: Richard Sutton; Doina Precup; Satinder Singh
options.define: Temporally extended actions are incorporated into a reinforcement-learning framework.
options.significance: Reusable skills can support hierarchical decisions and reduce the effective planning horizon.
options.limitation: Discovering useful skills and transferring them across tasks require mechanisms beyond the formalism itself.
options.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

aixi.title: AIXI joins universal induction and sequential decision
aixi.define: Algorithmic-probability prediction is combined with expected reward maximization in an idealized universal agent.
aixi.significance: General intelligence becomes a mathematical object connecting induction, Bayesian reasoning and reinforcement learning.
aixi.limitation: The original agent is not computable; environment assumptions, rewards and resource limits remain decisive.
aixi.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

causality.title: Structural causal models distinguish intervention
causality.define: Causality develops structural models and languages for interventions and counterfactuals.
causality.significance: An acting agent must reason about what its actions change, beyond correlations in observations.
causality.limitation: Identifying causal effects requires assumptions; more observational data do not eliminate that requirement.
causality.precision: The first edition appeared in 2000; the linked publisher record also covers the later edition.

inverse-rl.title: Inverse reinforcement learning infers objectives
inverse-rl.define: Algorithms infer reward-related explanations from observed behavior.
inverse-rl.significance: Learning what an expert is trying to achieve becomes distinct from learning which action to imitate.
inverse-rl.limitation: Multiple rewards may explain the same behavior, and human behavior is not perfectly optimal.
inverse-rl.precision: Year-level publication or historical milestone; later revisions do not change this marker.

neat.title: NEAT evolves neural structure and weights
neat.define: Neuroevolution combines historical markings, speciation and gradual complexification to search network structures and parameters.
neat.significance: Evolutionary and neural approaches become directly connected.
neat.limitation: The fitness environment still defines success; evolving a good controller does not establish unrestricted generality.
neat.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

bengio-lm.title: Neural language models learn distributed word representations
bengio-lm.define: A Neural Probabilistic Language Model jointly learns word representations and sequence probabilities.
bengio-lm.significance: Parameter sharing across similar contexts helps address the dimensionality of language modeling.
bengio-lm.limitation: Limited contexts and scale remain constraints; distributed representations do not by themselves solve grounding or reasoning.
bengio-lm.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

godel-machine.title: Godel Machines formalize provable self-rewriting
godel-machine.define: A theoretical machine searches for proofs that changes to its own code improve a specified utility before executing them.
godel-machine.significance: Self-improvement is connected to formal verification and explicit objectives.
godel-machine.limitation: Proof search and utility assumptions create substantial limits; this is not an observed unbounded improvement process.
godel-machine.precision: First preprint in 2003; later book and journal treatments are separate publications.

program-calo.title: CALO cognitive-assistant research program
program-calo.contributors: SRI International and collaborating research institutions; DARPA PAL
program-calo.define: The Cognitive Assistant that Learns and Organizes combines learning, reasoning, planning, interaction and personal information management in a sustained integration effort.
program-calo.significance: A practical assistant becomes a testbed for combining cognitive capabilities and learning from a user over time, well before contemporary language-model agents.
program-calo.limitation: Office-assistant tasks constrain its scope. Later Siri commercialization is a related transfer history, not evidence that the research assistant achieved AGI.
program-calo.precision: SRI describes five years of collaborative work beginning in 2003; 2003-2008 is the resulting year-level project window. Personnel, publication and commercialization timelines can extend beyond it.

darpa-challenge.title: Autonomous vehicles complete the DARPA desert challenge
darpa-challenge.contributors: Stanford Racing Team and other entrants
darpa-challenge.define: Multiple autonomous vehicles complete the 2005 desert course by integrating sensing, localization, planning and control.
darpa-challenge.significance: Robust systems emerge from coordinated components and feedback rather than one isolated algorithm.
darpa-challenge.limitation: A competition route differs from unrestricted public traffic; the unsuccessful 2004 event is a separate stage.
darpa-challenge.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

dbn.title: Deep belief networks revive multilayer learning
dbn.contributors: Geoffrey Hinton; Simon Osindero; Yee-Whye Teh
dbn.define: Layerwise training provides a practical approach to deep generative models under the training constraints of the period.
dbn.significance: Representation learning regains momentum and helps organize the emerging deep-learning community.
dbn.limitation: Most current large models do not use this specific algorithm; historical influence differs from present implementation.
dbn.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.

phase-deep-representations.title: Deep representation learning expands across tasks
phase-deep-representations.contributors: Multiple research groups; individual attribution appears in the linked milestones.
phase-deep-representations.define: Training methods, large datasets, accelerators and architectural changes support deeper learned representations in recognition, generation and sequence modeling.
phase-deep-representations.significance: Several interacting developments make deep learning a reusable research approach, connecting the 2006 revival to the Transformer milestone.
phase-deep-representations.limitation: The Transformer is a selected transition point; convolutional, recurrent and other neural methods continue afterward.
phase-deep-representations.precision: Editorial periodization anchored by the cited milestones. Boundaries identify a reading window, not a field-wide founding or termination date. Year-only boundaries do not claim exact days. The tradition continues beyond this selected phase.
phase-deep-representations.evidenceType: Editorial synthesis of the linked primary works

uct.title: UCT allocates Monte Carlo search effort
uct.define: Upper-confidence exploration is applied to tree-search branch selection.
uct.significance: Simulation budgets can be allocated adaptively, later complementing learned policy and value networks.
uct.limitation: The value of search depends on the simulator, problem structure and budget; it is not a complete intelligence architecture.
uct.precision: Year-level historical marker; the account distinguishes earlier development, publication and later deployment where relevant.
